title: Ring maps to the center construct linear structures
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive category [def-weil-preadditive-category]. Define its center $Z(\mathcal C)$ to consist of families $z=(z_X:X\to X)_{X\in\mathcal C}$ such that $z_Y\circ f=f\circ z_X$ for every $f:X\to Y$; equivalently these are natural endomorphisms of the identity functor. Addition and negation are componentwise, multiplication is composition, and the identity is $(\mathrm{id}_X)_X$; these operations make $Z(\mathcal C)$ a commutative ring. Let $B$ be a commutative ring. Any $B$-linear structure on $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-linear-category] gives a ring homomorphism $\rho:B\to Z(\mathcal C)$ with $\rho(b)_X=b\cdot\mathrm{id}_X$. Conversely, every ring homomorphism $\phi:B\to Z(\mathcal C)$ defines a $B$-linear structure on the fixed morphism groups by $b\cdot f=f\circ\phi(b)_X=\phi(b)_Y\circ f$ for $f:X\to Y$.
